newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil revives export guarantee scheme.
newsitem.headline: Brazil revives export guarantee scheme.

text.p: Brazil has resumed an export guarantee scheme to provide exporters with coverage from political and extraordinary risk, officials said.
A decree signed on Thursday by President Fernando Henrique Cardoso revivies the Export Credit Insurance system, which was put on hold in 1991 after the Treasury ran up losses.
A document produced jointly by the finance, planning and commerce and industry ministries said the system was "an important instrument to boost Brazilian exports."
The decree states that the National Treasury will cover exporters for 85 percent of the value of exporters' losses of up to $3.0 billion caused by political or extraordinary factors.
Operations involving payment over a maximum of eight years will automatically qualify for reimbursement although other cases may be negotiated.
A new, private insurance venture being set up by federal bank Banco do Brasil, which will act as a minority partner, will cover exporters for commercial risk.
